sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: An adjective that comes after the noun and says what the things are like takes the plural too: *A szék nagy.* → *A székek nagyok.* It follows the same harmony as nouns: *nagy* → *nagyok*, *szép* → *szépek*. After a vowel it only adds *-k*: *kicsi* → *kicsik*. You met this with people in unit 7 (*Ők magasak*); now it works for things as well.
English never changes 'big', so it is easy to forget the ending: *A székek nagy* is wrong. When the adjective is the answer to 'what are they like?', it agrees with a plural noun.
